Maya Partner Ops: Heads-up — GCP marketplace launch with Stratus Systems is scheduled for tomorrow 09:00 PT. Procurement just flagged one of their SKUs (STRATUS-XPU-64) as 'export-controlled' for EU shipments and the marketplace portal is rejecting POs that contain that classification. If unresolved, partner onboarding and first POs will fail and the launch will be delayed. Need owners and a short mitigation plan.
Liam Sales: Ugh, timeline is tight. Who initially flagged it — GCP or the partner?
Maya Partner Ops: GCP compliance flagged it during final PO validation. They returned a 403 with error: "sku_classification: restricted_export". marketplace-bot also emitted the rejection log.
marketplace-bot: PO-req-9987 rejected by GCP: 403 sku_classification=restricted_export region=EU
Sofia Legal: Can you paste the raw PO XML or normalized payload? We need to see which tag they're matching on. Might be a naming mismatch.
Maya Partner Ops: Snippet below from the normalized PO we send to GCP:
```xml
<LineItem>
  <SKU>STRATUS-XPU-64</SKU>
  <Quantity>10</Quantity>
  <Classification>ECCN:5A992</Classification>
</LineItem>
```
Maya Partner Ops: GCP is saying their whitelist expects a classification value of "EAR:EAR99" (their internal distribution code) for EU. Our feed currently sends ECCN values.
Derek Engineering: Quick technical mitigation — we can add a mapping rule in the PO normalization service to rewrite Classification:ECCN:* -> Classification:EAR:EAR99 for marketplace flows targeting EU. It's a small transform but it touches the signing pipeline and the canonical PO payload, so we need Legal/Partner OK.
Sofia Legal: We can approve an interim transform as a temporary mitigation if the partner signs an attestation confirming compliance and that we can map the value for marketplace POs. I'll draft a short attestation template now. cc @Liam Sales to get partner sign-off.
Liam Sales: Pinging Stratus contact — @Alex Stratus can you confirm Stratus can sign a one-off attestation to allow Redwood to map ECCN to EAR99 for EU marketplace orders? This is just for the marketplace pipeline, not a change to your export practices.
Alex Stratus: (from Stratus) We can sign that attestation. Our legal team wants to confirm wording first — please send draft.
Maya Partner Ops: Derek — estimate for hotfix + QA + deploy? Need it before 08:00 PT tomorrow to be safe.
Derek Engineering: Est: 3-4h dev, 1h QA, 30m deploy if everything goes smoothly. Could push tonight as a hotfix. Will open a PR and run staging tests.
Natalie Ops: I'll reserve a canary window overnight and prepare rollback steps. I'll also monitor the marketplace-bot ack stream and set alert thresholds.
marketplace-bot: deploy_check: mapping-rule preflight OK on staging. Previous test PO 12345 failed; retrying after mapping-rule applied.
Maya Partner Ops: Plan: Legal drafts attestation by EOD, partner signs ASAP, Derek implements mapping rule tonight, Natalie runs canary first thing, Liam keeps partner on expedited signing. I'll coordinate with GCP compliance for a quick revalidate once mapping is live.
Sofia Legal: Drafted attestation and uploaded to drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-link-attestation. Please review quickly.
Liam Sales: Partner signed at 21:07 PT. Attestation attached to the drive doc and emailed to GCP compliance.
Derek Engineering: Mapping-rule PR merged and deployed to staging at 23:30 PT. Ran test PO: now accepted by GCP for EU region in staging.
marketplace-bot: rollout: mapping-rule v1 deployed to production at 00:05 PT. Monitoring acceptance stream for PO-req-* patterns.
Natalie Ops: Canary run succeeded. No regressions observed. Monitoring token and ack rates; setting 5m alerts for new PO rejects.
Maya Partner Ops: Launch can proceed as planned. Thank you all for the quick turnaround. We'll do a short postmortem tomorrow to decide on the long-term fix: either normalize onboarding docs to require EAR-coded classification or add a normalized classification table in our SKU onboarding flow. :tada:
Sofia Legal: +1 — I'll add a contract addendum template so future SIs/partners supply both ECCN and EAR where necessary.
Liam Sales: Great teamwork, folks. :rocket:
